- Full recursive scan of every collection in core.json for the string `create-thrall`: exactly two owners, `spells/create-thrall` and `classes/necromancer`. Nothing else.
- `grep -rln "create-thrall" scripts/ src/ public/` → only migration dumps, `public/ast/*`, `core.json`, `core-descriptions.json`, `idmap.json`. **No engine registry, no mode, no backfill entry.**

- `src/rules/advancement.ts` has `necromancer` and `necromancer-reaper` tables (lines 221, 243) — proficiency rows only, class-only, no ability grants.

THE DECISIVE COMPARISON — the app already uses the right carrier on this archetype's siblings
- `feats/thrall-charger` → `focusSpells: ["thrall-charge"]`
- `feats/necrotic-bomber` → `focusSpells: ["necrotic-bomb"]`

confirmed.evidence:
CONFIRMED — I could not refute it. Every escape hatch checked and found empty.

1. The printed text does contain the clause, verbatim. `public/core-descriptions.json` → `feats['verduran-shadow-dedication'].d`: "...You can substitute your proficiency in Survival for your proficiency in Stealth when meeting feat prerequisites and gaining additional benefits from feats for being an expert, master, or legendary in Stealth; however, unless you also fulfill the Stealth prerequisite, you can only use those feats in forest terrain. While in forests, you can use your Survival modifier in place of your Stealth modifier when you Avoid Notice, Hide, Sneak, or would use Stealth to roll initiative." So it is two distinct mechanics, not prose restating one — and it is mechanical, not flavour.

2. The record carries only the roll-swap. `public/core.json` → the feat has exactly one `skillSubstitutions` entry `{use:'survival', forSkill:'stealth', when:'when you Avoid Notice, Hide, Sneak, or would use Stealth to roll initiative'}`, plus `prerequisites:['trained in Stealth','trained in Survival']`. No second entry, no `dataWarning`.

3. No overlay carrier. A full recursive key walk of `scripts/data/effect-backfill.json` for 'verduran' returns nothing.

4. No hard-coded engine branch. Repo-wide grep for the id across `src/` and `scripts/` hits only `src/rules/featGrantsAuto.ts:570` (`'verduran-shadow-dedication': { skills: { survival: 'expert' } }` — that is the "You become an expert in Survival" sentence, a raise-to-rank grant, unrelated) plus audit/worklist JSON. Nothing in modes.ts, advancement.ts, situationalBonuses.ts, featGrants.ts.

5. No general engine rule covers it. `skillSubstitutions` has exactly two readers — `src/rules/derive.ts:412` (the resolver) → `skillSubstituteFor` at `derive.ts:440`, consumed by `deriveSkill` at `derive.ts:542` for the displayed skill row, and `src/rules/explain.ts:535` for the breakdown. `grep -n "skillSubstitution|substitut" src/rules/build.ts` returns only unrelated comment prose (class-archetype feature substitution, formula token substitution) — `buildCharacter` never applies a substitution to `character.proficiencies.skills`.

6. The prerequisite check reads the raw rank. `checkPrerequisites` (`src/rules/build.ts:7654`) resolves rank via `rankOf`: `if ((SKILLS as readonly string[]).includes(target)) return character.proficiencies.skills[target as SkillId] ?? 'untrained';` — no substitution consulted. It has `content` in scope but never calls the resolver.

7. Also, `skillSubstituteFor` could not deliver it even if it were wired in: it hard-skips every entry with a `when` (`if (s.when || s.forSkill !== key) continue;`), and this entry has one. The type doc at `src/rules/types.ts:895-914` states the design intent explicitly — a conditional substitution "must NOT silently replace the skill's number... doesn't replace Medicine for uses of the skill other than Treat Wounds **or for feat prerequisites**". So the shape `{use, forSkill, when}` deliberately has no route to the prereq check; there is no field it could travel on. Grep for `prereqSub|prerequisiteSub|countsAsRank|proficiencySubstitution|forPrereq|countsAs|treatedAs` across `src/rules/types.ts` and `src/` returns nothing.

8. It is not a menu-options complaint — the block is real and enforced. `src/builder/Builder.tsx:389` builds `featPrereqChar = buildCharacter(build, ovContent)` (raw proficiencies), and `Builder.tsx:2434` (`featIneligible`, the hide-ineligible predicate) and `Builder.tsx:2550` (`renderRow` → `unmet`) both gate on `checkPrerequisites`. An unmet row is dimmed and only takeable via the Overrides "Take anyway" escape hatch, which is a deliberate rule-break switch, not a model of this feat.

9. The block bites in practice. 36 feats in `public/core.json` carry a prerequisite line exactly matching `^(expert|master|legendary) in Stealth$` — bellflower-dedication, forest-stealth, silent-sting, anticipate-ambush, fanes-escape (expert); shadowdancer-dedication, camouflage, ashen-veil, wardens-step, shooters-camouflage, eclipsed-vitality (master); shadow-self (legendary); and 24 more. Every one of those lines IS enforced by the rank branch, so an expert-Survival / trained-Stealth Verduran Shadow is wrongly blocked from all 36. Note `forest-stealth` is itself a Verduran Shadow archetype feat gated at "expert in Stealth" — i.e. the archetype's own feat chain is unreachable by exactly the character the dedication is written for.

10. Shared lane, not a one-off: `feats/snarecrafter-dedication` carries the identical unmodelled shape (`{use:'survival', forSkill:'crafting', when:'for all prerequisites and functions of feats from this archetype'}`). 33 records total carry `skillSubstitutions`; these two state the prerequisite clause outright.

Secondary observation (not the claim, but adjacent and real): the modelled `when` string drops the printed "While in forests" gate — the roll-swap is authored as unconditional-in-wording where the book restricts it to forest terrain.

- `musket-staff-of-void` — name "Musket Staff of Void", same level/price/bulk, same aonId `equipment-3588`, same `heldSpells` and `counters`, plus `itemType: "weapon"`, simple/firearm, 1d6 piercing, range 70, reload 1, hands 2, usage held-in-two-hands, traits concussive + fatal-d10. No `grantsItems`.

`public/core-descriptions.json` settles that they are one item, not two: the `-the-void` entry's description is the raw AoN page scrape, header furniture and all — "Musket Staff of the Void \nSource NPC Core pg. 81\nPrice 100 gp\nUsage held in 2 hands\nBulk 1 \n\n Base Weapon Flintlock Musket \n\n…" — while `musket-staff-of-void` carries the same prose cleaned, italicised, with `r` descRefs to Reinforced Stock / Void Warp / Grim Tendrils. Identical body text, identical spell list.

**2. Refutation attempt: is the duplicate hidden by the loader's dedupe chokepoint?** No. I ran `findDuplicateIds` / `findUmbrellaIds` / `findCombinationFormIds` from `src/data/index.ts` over the shipped `public/core.json` via jiti, then `listValues(content, content.items)` — the exact chokepoint every user-facing list goes through (`src/data/index.ts:387`). Result:
```
musket-staff-of-the-void | dup: false | umbrella: false | combForm: false
musket-staff-of-void     | dup: false | umbrella: false | combForm: false
VISIBLE musket staff rows:
  - musket-staff-of-force        | itemType= weapon    | damage= {"dice":1,"die":"d6","type":"piercing"}
  - musket-staff-of-the-void     | itemType= equipment | damage= undefined
  - musket-staff-of-void         | itemType= weapon    | damage= {"dice":1,"die":"d6","type":"piercing"}
```
All three rules structurally miss it: neither id is `aon-`-prefixed (so the prefix rule at `src/data/index.ts:155` can't fire); `dedupeKey` normalises to "musketstaffofthevoid" vs "musketstaffofvoid" so the exact-name rule can't pair them; `gradeSpellingDuplicates` needs a GRADE_WORD in the name and returns `null` for both; the umbrella rule requires an unpriced record and this one has 100 gp. Neither `NEAR_DUPLICATE_IDS` nor `REMASTER_REPRINT_IDS` lists it (grep of `src/` for "musket-staff" returns exactly one hit, `src/rules/itemAliases.ts:212`). So the shop and every item picker offer both rows.

**3. Refutation attempt: does some carrier make the equipment record wieldable anyway?** No. `src/rules/derive.ts:3819` — `export function deriveStrike(...)  { const item = db.items[inv.itemId]; if (!item || item.itemType !== 'weapon') return null;` — and the wield toggle itself is gated at `src/sheet/InventoryTab.tsx:77-78` (`itemType === 'weapon'`). Grep of `src/` and `scripts/data/` for both ids finds only `itemAliases.ts:212` and three `effect-backfill.json` entries (lines 53816 `heldSpells`, 53829 `counters`, 135817 `grantsItems`) plus one `edition` entry for the sibling at 115060 — no registry, no `modes.ts` branch, no hard-coded engine path.

**4. Refutation attempt: is the rune-mirroring clause covered by a general rule?** No. `src/rules/attachments.ts` has no rune sharing, and `isAttachable` requires a usage starting `affixed|attached` — `reinforced-stock` (`itemType: weapon`, martial club, 1d4 B, usage `held-in-one-hand`, trait `attached-to-crossbow-or-firearm`) fails it, so the stock can't even be affixed to the musket. ...
let rank: ProficiencyRank = 'trained';
for (const other of feats) {
  const up = content.feats[other.featId]?.classDcRank;
